Notice of Lien
A Notice of Lien is a correspondence from the health insurance provider to the law firm, indicating that they may have settled claims associated with the accident and are expecting reimbursement at the conclusion of the case.

Notice of Lien
This represents a lien on the settlement. The health insurance subrogation company waits for the law firm to reimburse the health insurance provider once the case is resolved.

Final Subrogation Lien Letter
A Final Subrogation Lien Letter is a formal communication sent by an insurance company or healthcare provider to a third party (often another insurance company, attorney, or liable party) requesting reimbursement for expenses that have been paid on behalf of the insured or injured party. The letter confirms the final amount of the lien and outlines the subrogation claim, which is the process by which the insurer seeks to recover the costs they have already covered.

After Bills Have Been Submitted
A Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) is a systematic approach used to evaluate the financial and non-financial advantages (benefits) and disadvantages (costs) of a decision, project, or policy. It helps decision-makers assess whether the benefits of a certain action outweigh the costs and determine the most financially sound option.

After Bills Have Been Submitted
REVIEW the lien again to ensure all RELEVANT bills are on the lien. Request to remove irrelevant bills. REMEMBER to weigh the cost-benefit analysis of the amount of the bill and the work that you would need to put in to remove the bill. Pick your battles, some bills are not worth fighting as they would cost you more in time to remove.

Once you have received the Final Subrogation Lien Ledger
You can request a reduction of the subrogation lien amount, with potential outcomes being:
Approved Reduction: The lien reduction request is approved and you can pay the reduced amount.
Rejected Request for Lien Reduction: The request was denied.
Counter Offer of Lien Reduction: Health insurance companies may propose a different amount or request settlement information, which you can choose to provide or accept.

Subrogation Lien Ledger
Ensure that the DATES and SERVICES are linked to the incident. Review your records to confirm whether all bills are accounted for or if any are missing. Depending on the situation, you may choose to request the bills and records or not. This typically depends on whether you require them for the demand. Research the providers online to ascertain their affiliations and see if they are connected to the collision.

Subrogation Lien Ledger
Check the lien to determine if any bills are absent. Additionally, ask for any bills you need to examine to ensure that all figures are accurate. In certain situations, it may be best not to request the bills and records, especially if the policy limits have been exceeded and you need to interplead the funds.
